result:
I've verified round 112 in a real headless Chromium (143), and every row has run. A's change is correct: line 4 of doc 096 is the only difference from `6abd3f3`, and the frozen file list matched at the start and at the end. So `taskStatus` is **PASS** and `browserVerified`/`realVerified` are **true**. Of the four Mediums, one closes (C-R27-01), three come out FAIL, and for two of those (C-R6-02, C-R8-01) a one-frame measurement artefact is behind most of the drift failures, so B needs to decide.

| Finding | §5 outcome | What I measured |
|---|---|---|
| **C-R27-01** (video sync with level meters running) | **PASS → closed** | 3/3 valid runs, worst drift 15.6–16.0 ms against the 30.1 ms limit, no hard seeks. |
| **C-R8-01** (detail panel open, music clip selected) | **FAIL, no app attribution** | 0/3 under the rule as written (details below). |
| **C-R6-02** (panel open, nothing selected; first Play after load) | **FAIL, no app attribution** | Drift: 0/3 with a clip selected, 1/3 with nothing selected. First-Play timing check: 1/3. |
| **A-R38-REVIEW-TOUCH** | **FAIL → bounded A round** with the pre-agreed fix | Volume, Pan and Master all jump on a touch press, 3/3 each. |

None of the drift runs had a stall, a long frame or dropped video frames, so none of these failures can be blamed on app scripts.

**Decision for B (C-R6-02 and C-R8-01):** in 8 of 9 runs, the drift failure is a single sample at the cut between the two video clips. In that frame the second clip is already showing while the ruler still reads 5.99. The rule as written scores that as about 6 s of drift. What the user actually sees is the cut about 18 ms early, roughly one frame. Every other sample stays at or below 37 ms. Task §3 names this one-frame skew as a known limit. If that one sample is matched to the next clip instead, all 9 runs pass. I wrote that correction after seeing the 6 s numbers, so I report it next to the verdict and did not use it for the verdict.

**First-Play timing (RF5-3):** in N2 and N3, the app starts the video about 22.5 ms before the audio start point, and the allowed window is ±16.7 ms. In this cloud browser the audio clock advances in irregular steps of 8.7–31.9 ms. The audio start point has to be estimated from the ruler, which follows that clock, so the estimate can be off by more than the window. There is also a pattern I can't confirm: with the detail panel open, 5 of 6 first Plays fail; with it collapsed, 0 of 4 do. B has to judge whether that counts as the cost following app state.

**Touch:** a single touch moved Volume from 1.00 to 0.09, Pan from centre to 50, and Master from 0 dB to −54.5 dB. Each jump also adds an Undo step, so a stray tap really changes the mix. The test is valid because the Zoom slider (the positive control) jumped too, and a mouse press at the same point does not jump.

**Other rows:**
- **Auth protection (G112-3): PASS.** `/studio-lab` opens the demo, `/studio/middle-east` shows "Sign in required" with no audio loaded, and the token endpoint returns 401. The fake-Bearer 403 sub-check is BLOCKED because the backend isn't available in the cloud.
- **Network and console: PASS.** Across 34 sessions there were no requests to forbidden hosts, no `Authorization` headers, no hydration errors and no page errors.
- **H.264 (diagnostic only):** the MP4 really plays in this build. Its runs show the same single sample at the clip cut.

**Deviations:**
- The demo library has no CZABA-hero stem, so the stems lane used the "ღამის პულსი · პულსი" stem.
- In the meter check, the stems meter can't move in the first second because that clip starts at 2 s. It moves from 2.0 s.
- My first three "nothing selected" runs still had a clip selected, because the click to deselect landed off-screen. I set them aside without counting them and re-ran that layout as a block, not alternated with the other layouts.

I changed nothing under `store/`, and I didn't run the gate rows (tests, typecheck, build, verify).

Files are in `/home/runner/czaba-project/tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- `c-round-112.md`
- `c-round-112.json`
- `c-round-112/env.json`, and runs, tools and screenshots under `c-round-112/`
